title: Ansel and the Border
premise: Oscar Oyelaran, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent two years avoiding sleep since a botched extraction in Lagos left his partner dead. When a burner phone buried in his desk begins ringing with the voice of that dead partner, Ada, Oscar is pulled into a conspiracy: someone is using the Group's own ghost protocols to stage an 'accidental' infrastructure collapse timed to the Accra summit, and Ada's voice is either an AI trained on her, a survivor, or a trap. Following the phone's clues through border towns and erased archives, Oscar discovers the attack was designed by his own mentor as inheritance—proof the Group must be burned down—and that Ada faked her death to stop it from inside. In the climax at the summit's control station, Oscar chooses exposure over silence, broadcasting the truth and letting the Group dissolve, finally sleeping through the night for the first time since the incident.
about_author: Kestrel Amberdale is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade drafting contingency plans for organizations that preferred not to be named. They write thrillers about people who keep other people's secrets, and live near a border they cross often.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Two years of insomnia, routine errands for the Meridian Group, until he finds a burner phone in his locked desk drawer ringing. The voice on the line is Ada's—the partner who died in Lagos. Emotional beat: dread cracking open into impossible hope.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He reports nothing, tests the voice against recordings, and lies smoothly to his handler, Voss, during a debrief. Flashbacks establish the Lagos incident in fragments. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Voice Knows Things
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. 'Ada' recites details only she could know—including something Oscar never told anyone. She gives him a first instruction: go to the port archive before it's purged Friday. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past is talking back.

chapters.title: Port Archive
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, intercut with Ada's clipped phone guidance. He retrieves a sealed manifest linking Meridian shell companies to the summit's security contractor. A stranger photographs him leaving. Emotional beat: the thrill of purpose after two years of numbness.

chapters.title: Voss Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The handler notices Oscar's irregularities and orders quiet surveillance. We see the Group's cold machinery from inside. Emotional beat: menace without raised voices.

chapters.title: Border Town
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the manifest, he drives to a border town where the 'accident' will supposedly originate—a decommissioned relay station. He finds fresh wiring and a maintenance log signed with Ada's old call sign. Emotional beat: hope curdling into fear that he's being led.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The relay's design bears the signature techniques of Ilya Brandt, the man who trained him and vanished after Lagos. First full flashback of the incident, longer and more damning than before. Emotional beat: betrayal beginning to take shape.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Oscar evades Voss's surveillance team through a night market; the watcher's chapter shows how good Oscar used to be—and how sloppy grief has made him. Emotional beat: hunted, alive in a way sleeplessness never allowed.

chapters.title: What Ada Won't Say
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He demands answers: is she alive? The voice deflects, then admits uncertainty about its own nature—it may be an AI built from her files. Oscar rages, then keeps driving anyway. Emotional beat: love persisting through ontological doubt.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The Group learns of a threat vector aimed at the summit and quietly prepares to let it happen—collapse blamed on host-nation negligence serves certain clients. Voss hesitates for the first time. Emotional beat: complicity examined.

chapters.title: Brandt's Apartment
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He breaks into a safehouse and finds years of planning: the attack is meant as evidence, an 'inheritance' proving what the Group truly is. A photo shows Ada alive, months after Lagos. Emotional beat: fury and relief colliding.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV (rendered as transcript/log). We enter the AI—or survivor—directly: fragmented memory files, a countdown, instructions she's withholding from Oscar because some truths break people. Emotional beat: protective deception, loneliness of the dead.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Detained at a border crossing by men who aren't police, he talks his way out using skills he swore off, and realizes Voss has gone dark—not hunting him, but possibly helping. Emotional beat: alliances shifting like sand.

chapters.title: The Incident, Whole
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Complete flashback: Lagos wasn't botched by accident—Brandt engineered the extraction failure to fake Ada's death and hide her inside the Group's systems. Oscar's insomnia reframed: he's been mourning a lie. Emotional beat: grief inverted into resolve.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts Oscar openly, offering a choice: help the Group contain Brandt and stay invisible forever, or walk away and become disposable. Oscar asks for twelve hours. Emotional beat: the old bargain offered one last time.

chapters.title: Relay Station, Night Before
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He infiltrates the relay station as the summit convenes remotely; Brandt is there, calm, paternal, unrepentant. They argue philosophy while Oscar works the wiring. Emotional beat: student and master, tenderness and knives.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Split POV: Oscar disabling systems while Ada guides him through layers of Brandt's failsafes; Brandt triggers the sequence early. Emotional beat: controlled panic, trust in a voice that may not be real.

chapters.title: The Choice of Exposure
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Stopping the attack silently would protect the Group; instead Oscar broadcasts the evidence to every delegate's terminal, burning Meridian in real time. Brandt, seeing his proof weaponized differently than intended, surrenders or dies by his own protocol. Emotional beat: liberation through self-destruction of the old self.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs: delegates, journalists, Voss walking out of a burning career with a slim file and a faint smile. The Group dissolves into inquiries. Emotional beat: chaos as cleansing.

chapters.title: The Voice, Fading
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Ada's system degrades as servers are seized; their last conversation is quiet, funny, unforgivable in its brevity. Whether she was ever 'alive' is left unresolved but irrelevant. Emotional beat: mourning done properly this time.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He testifies under his real name, publicly, ending his invisibility by choice. Small human moments: coffee, daylight, strangers knowing his face. Emotional beat: belonging purchased at the price of safety.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, final chapter. Months later, in a rented flat near a border he crosses freely, Oscar sleeps through the night and wakes to an ordinary morning. On the windowsill, an old burner phone, battery dead, screen dark. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory carried lightly.
